1622607912173465610 [2023-02-06] @IaimforGOAT 💜 1
Let's start by saying I have a hard time trusting other to help me manage my emotions, so I end up doing it solo (I wish it wasn't like that but alas), so sometimes I am processing something really hard and it changes me in some ways.
↓
1622607915474472960 [2023-02-06] @IaimforGOAT 💜 1
For example, my voice gets a heavier and more aggressive/tense tone, also somewhat sarcastic (???). EVEN WHEN I DON'T WANT TO!
↓
1622607918238470144 [2023-02-06] @IaimforGOAT 💜 1
So imagine a scenario where someone asks me something, like they had a problem and ask me to go get their kids at school. There's no problem, I can do it just fine and I will like to see them and spend a bit of time with them, so I say I'll do it.
↓
1622607921107333120 [2023-02-06] @IaimforGOAT 💜 1
But if I am in one of those times where I am processing stuff, when they talk to me (because they feel bad it was like 2h or 3 before it had to be done) I will reply smth like "no problem, I had no plans" and it comes across with that tone!! 😭
↓
1622607924378980359 [2023-02-06] @IaimforGOAT 💜 1
And it hurts, because I don't intent to come across that way but it's like I have no bandwidth to modulate my voice and it is stuck in that tone because of the things I am processing...
↓
1622607927801438211 [2023-02-06] @IaimforGOAT 💜 1
So yeah after these interactions I feel super bad, because there's 0% chance they won't infer something from the way I spoke and they'll think it is related to the ask, which it is not! =(
↓
1622607931245043714 [2023-02-06] @IaimforGOAT 💜 1
Not only will this create a misunderstanding, but it will probably have consequences like make them update on negatively on my willingness to help in similar situations, which, again, I didn't meant to do because I couldn't even modulate my tone properly to that situation =|
↓

    Bill of Rights for Friends
    
    * What does she want and need in a friendship? (Trust, reliability, loyalty, telling you when they're angry with you in a respectful way)
    * What are her rights in a friendship? (To be treated respectfully, with kindness and honesty)
    * What are her responsibilities in a friendship? (To treat her friends ethically)
    * What would a friend have to do or be like for her to end the friendship? (Not listen to her, not honor her values and ethics)
    * Under what circumstances would she go to an adult for help with a problem with a friend? (When the problem feels too big to handle alone)
    * What are her friends' rights and responsibilities in the friendship? (To listen even when it's not easy to hear)
    
    Then ask the hardest question: How do her experiences with her friends compare to her Bill of Rights? If they aren't similar, why does she have those friendships?
    
    If and when your daughter makes the decision that her friend(s) aren't right for her, it'll be a very lonely time for her. She may know that she has made the right decision in ending a friendship, but that'll be only a small comfort. rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents a **Hermeneutic Arc** around childhood trauma's manifestation in adult relationships, anchored by Visa's mariachi band metaphor (the boundary object). The discourse evolves from a playful meme (2019-2020) into deep somatic/psychological excavation (2021-2025), primarily through Yatharth's serial self-analysis threads. The arc is **dialectical-turned-constructive**: early threads are introspective monologues, later ones synthesize frameworks (Patrick Teahan videos, Queen Bees book, Malcolm's expectations taxonomy). The community validates subjective experiences of hypervigilance, conflict-aversion, and emotional regulation struggles, creating shared vocabulary around 'forecasting,' 'intensity mismatch,' and 'being allowed to be sad.' High cohesion (Yatharth as central node with Visa/Malcolm/others providing scaffolding), medium-high utility (actionable frameworks for recognizing trauma patterns), but longevity penalty: most evolution happens 2021-2023, then repetition/application phase.

essential_tweets.annotation: The Artifact: Visa's mariachi band metaphor establishes the boundary object—trauma as an uninvited performance that interrupts self-inquiry
Reframe: Visa introduces the idea that trauma processing doesn't have to be 'morose and clinical'—you can have fun with it
First Application: Yatharth begins using the metaphor to mark moments of self-discovery (socks/abundance scarcity beliefs)
Core Insight: The 'forecasting' framework—hypervigilance as constantly predicting social threats to prevent punishment/abandonment
Somatic Connection: Links forecasting to physical tension and introduces the idea that 'the world can be gentle'
Permission Structure: Not feeling guilty for being sad—challenging the belief that emotions require immediate resolution
Theoretical Synthesis: Malcolm Ocean's 3 types of expectations framework (anticipations/entitlements/commitments)—resolving codependency confusion
Practical Tool: Queen Bees 'Bill of Rights for Friends' as concrete vocabulary for what's reasonable to ask in relationships
Meta-Pattern: 'Why isn't the obvious advice working?'—recognizing that trauma creates implementation gaps, not knowledge gaps
Endgame Wisdom: Nosilverv's distillation—conflict-seeking people abuse conflict-aversive people; becoming comfortable with conflict is the exit
